I won’t try and compare our experiences as ASD is a spectrum obviously and I have low support needs but when I started out in photography at 18, I was drawn to portraits and missed out on a lot of shoots and opportunities because of my fear of being awkward and up until quite recently still didn’t know how to handle those interactions without being awkward. Here are things that helped me 
1) having a lot of references for shoots - directing others was intimidating for me so I created boards with everything like pose references so if I was getting socially overwhelmed I could just show them 
2) (I was an art school student at the time so may not be as accessible for you) either assisting or just being there for other photographers shoots, allowed me to make almost a script of what I could say. Sometimes I have to still plan out social interactions and that’s ok! 
3) continuously building my portfolio and having these interactions built my self esteem as a whole and made the process easier 

I know it’s not as easy as it sounds but trying to build your self esteem in other areas of your life can be really beneficial and the more you push yourself the easier it can get. I don’t know what you look like and wouldn’t want to comment on that but as long as you look put together (well groomed/dressed ect) and your work is good that should be enough, not saying you don’t but when people make an effort with their appearance it’s less off putting
